newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No ransom for Chechnen kidnappers -Italian envoy.
newsitem.headline: No ransom for Chechnen kidnappers -Italian envoy.

text.p: Italy's ambassador to Moscow said on Tuesday his government was ready to negotiate with the unknown group which kidnapped an Italian press photographer in rebel Chechnya but firmly ruled out paying a ransom.
"Governments cannot, do not wish to and should not pay ransoms," Ambassador Emanuele Scammacca told Russian Television.
Photographer Mauro Galligani, 55, who works for the news weekly "Panorama", was seized by four armed and masked men on Sunday outside the Chechen capital Grozny.

"Bad examples are tempting and having once succeeded in such an enterprise kidnappers will repeat it again and again," the ambassador said. "We will not put down the phone. But the talks should be fair."

Scamacco said Italian diplomats were in touch with Russian and Chechen separatist authorities. Chechen officials said they were doing all they could to stamp out lawless bands who have staged a number of recent kidnappings, apparently for money.
Two Russian television journalists were released unharmed last week after several weeks in capivity.
Chechen Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev said his forces were working on Galligani's case but he criticised the journalist for not notifying the local security forces in advance of his movements.
Moscow, which pulled out its troops last autumn after a bloody but unsuccessful two-year intervention against separatist rebels, refuses to countenance Chechen sovereignty.
Negotiations continued on Wednesday between officials from the two sides. Chechen Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov met Russian Security Council Secretary Ivan Rybkin near Moscow.
Both men told Russian Television the talks went smoothly.

Interfax news agency quoted local police in the southern Russian region of Stavropol as saying Russian Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov had met Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov in the region. But Interior Ministry officials in Moscow could not confirm the report.
